name: epona
author: Hybrasyl Maintainers <hybrasyl@eris.co>
_desktopNameNote: Read by electron-builder, not by npm. Electron uses it as the Linux app_id /
WM_CLASS, and linux.syncDesktopName makes the installed .desktop filename match.
Lowercase 'epona' on purpose: the Linux executable name is appInfo.sanitizedName
lowercased, so this is the one spelling that makes the .desktop filename, its
StartupWMClass and Electron's own app_id all agree. 'Epona.desktop' would look
tidier beside productName and would break the association it exists to create.

scripts.validate: npm run lint:check && npm run format:check && npm test

_dependenciesNote: electron-builder copies EVERY `dependencies` entry into app.asar verbatim.
Only main and preload are externalized (externalizeDepsPlugin); the renderer
config has none, so vite already bundles every UI library into out/renderer.
Anything renderer-only listed here therefore ships TWICE. Keep this list to
what main/preload actually require at run time.
da-win32 is easy to get wrong: it is loaded via createRequire(), not a static
import, AND it is rollup-external, so it is NOT bundled and must be present in
node_modules at run time. A grep for import/require will not find it.
_overridesNote: brace-expansion <=5.0.7 carries a high-severity DoS advisory (GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg),
reaching us only through dev tooling. Nothing that ships is affected.
SCOPED TO THE 1.x MAJOR ON PURPOSE. The advisory is patched WITHIN every major --
1.1.18, 2.1.4, 3.0.6, 5.0.9 -- so every consumer can stay on the line it was written
against. Only the 1.x copies (pinned by minimatch 3.x) were ever vulnerable here; the
2.x and 5.x copies already sat on patched versions. npm resolves a name@range selector
against the RESOLVED version, so minimatch 3.x gets a callable default export while
minimatch 10.x keeps the 5.x copy whose named `expand` it imports.
DO NOT widen this to a bare `brace-expansion` override. 5.x changed its export shape
-- 1.x/2.x are `module.exports = expand`, 5.x is `module.exports = { expand, ... }` --
and minimatch 3.x does `var expand = require('brace-expansion')` then calls it. A
global override breaks EVERY minimatch 3.x consumer: eslint, @eslint/eslintrc,
eslint-plugin-react, @electron/asar, dir-compare and glob. It fails only for a pattern
CONTAINING BRACES, because minimatch 3.x short-circuits braceExpand otherwise -- so it
hides. @electron/asar and dir-compare run during packaging, where a passing build
proves nothing unless the globs happened to carry braces.
GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr, GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7 and GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p (2026-10) then cover
5.x copies move inside their own ranges (2.1.7, 5.0.12) with npm update; no selector for
them is needed while their consumers' ranges reach the fixed versions.
Nothing to unwind later: the selector stops matching once the last minimatch 3.x
consumer is gone.
global-agent@3 -> ^4.1.3 (GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c, 8 moderate findings in one chain). The
advisory is on sprintf-js, and its range is every version, so no sprintf-js release fixes
it. The path is app-builder-lib -> @electron/get@3 -> global-agent@3 -> roarr -> sprintf-js.
electron-builder 26.17 and the 27 alpha still pin @electron/get@3. global-agent 4 removes
roarr and keeps the same CommonJS entry and the same `bootstrap` export, which is the one
call @electron/get makes (dist/cjs/proxy.js), and only when ELECTRON_GET_USE_PROXY is set.
Build time only: Electron itself uses @electron/get@5, so nothing here ships. Remove it
when electron-builder 27, on @electron/get@5, is stable. (creidhne and taliesin, HTOO-570.)
_allowScriptsNote: npm 12 skips every dependency install script that this block does not approve, with only
a warning and exit 0. Approvals are by name, not by version (HTOO-542). esbuild selects its
platform binary. fsevents is the macOS file watcher behind vite and rollup; it is optional
and absent off macOS, so a Windows npm ci never lists it. electron-winstaller is listed as
false only to mark it reviewed: it serves Squirrel installers, which Epona does not ship.
electron is not listed: since Electron 42 it has no install script. The project's OWN
postinstall runs install-electron first (a no-op when the binary is there), because
electron-vite dev reads the binary path without require(), so a fresh clone could not run
npm run dev (HTOO-553). npm 12 does not gate the project's own scripts.
packages/da-win32 is not listed: npm 12 does not gate a workspace member (npm
install-scripts ls lists nothing), and postinstall rebuilds it in any case.
